In each stretchable region, a plurality of elongated elastic members is disposed between two sheet layers. The elastic members are arranged at predetermined intervals in the front-back direction of the diaper. Each elastic member extends in the width direction and includes two fixed end portions that are secured to the sheet layers. A portion of each elastic member located between the fixed end portions is left unattached to the sheet layers.

The two sheet layers are joined together by welding to form sheet bonding sections. These sheet bonding sections are provided between adjacent elastic members within the stretchable regions.

In the stretchable regions, the sheet bonding sections are arranged so that they do not protrude from the side seal portions. This configuration helps maintain the desired stretchability and fit of the diaper while preventing unnecessary protrusions near the side seal areas.

An underpants-type disposable diaper is provided with an improved structure in its stretchable side regions to enhance fit, comfort, and overall wearing performance. The diaper includes a front waist region, a rear waist region, and a crotch region extending between them, with the front and rear waist regions joined together at opposite side portions to form a waist opening and a pair of leg openings. In the side regions of the diaper, a plurality of elastic members are arranged so as to extend in the width direction of the diaper, thereby allowing the side portions to stretch and contract around the wearer’s body.

Each elastic member is disposed between two sheet layers forming the side region. Unlike structures in which the elastic members are continuously bonded along their entire length, the elastic members in this diaper are fixed primarily at their end portions. Between adjacent elastic members, sheet bonding sections are formed by welding or otherwise joining the two sheet layers together. These bonding sections are positioned in the spaces between neighboring elastic members and help stabilize the layered sheet structure without restricting the stretchability of the elastic members themselves.

Because the elastic members are not excessively bonded over their full length, the side regions can expand and contract smoothly in response to the wearer’s movement and body shape. At the same time, the welded sheet bonding sections prevent the two sheet layers from separating or shifting, thereby improving the structural integrity of the side regions. This arrangement provides a balance between secure construction and flexibility.

The diaper also includes side seal portions where the front and rear waist regions are joined to one another. In conventional structures, bonding sections or welded portions in the stretchable side regions may protrude outward from the side seals, creating stiffness, discomfort, or an undesirable appearance. In the present structure, the bonding sections between the elastic members are arranged so that they do not protrude from the side seal portions. As a result, the side seals remain neat and compact, and the diaper can be worn comfortably without hard or projecting portions pressing against the wearer’s skin.

This construction helps maintain the elasticity of the side regions while improving the reliability of the sheet bonding. The elastic members provide the necessary stretch and contraction for a snug fit around the waist and hips, while the welded sheet bonding sections reinforce the side region without interfering with elastic performance. Consequently, the diaper can better conform to the wearer’s body, reduce looseness or sagging, and improve comfort during movement.

Overall, the underpants-type disposable diaper achieves an improved side-region construction by positioning widthwise elastic members between two sheet layers, fixing only their end portions, and forming welded bonding sections between adjacent elastic members. This design prevents unwanted protrusion of bonding sections from the side seals, preserves stretchability, and enhances both the fit and comfort of the diaper.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps make meaning clear. When we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a specific book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word brings focus and precision to communication. It points to something known, unique, or already mentioned. For example, “the sun” refers to the one sun we all know, and “the answer” suggests a particular answer being discussed.

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it appears constantly in English because it helps connect ideas and guide understanding. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. In this way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract-style description for an underpants-type disposable diaper invention involving outer members, stretchable regions near side seals, elastic members between sheet layers, and welded bonding sections.
counterfactuals.output:
An underpants-type disposable diaper includes an absorbent main body and an exterior member forming a waist-opening and a pair of leg-openings. The exterior member has a front outer member and a back outer member joined to each other at laterally opposite side seal portions. At least one of the front outer member and the back outer member includes a plurality of sheet layers and a plurality of elastic members disposed between the sheet layers so as to form a stretchable region in the waist or torso direction.

In regions adjacent to the side seal portions, the sheet layers are bonded together by welded bonding sections. The welded bonding sections are arranged so as to secure the elastic members between the sheet layers while maintaining desired stretchability of the stretchable region. The welded bonding sections may be provided at intervals along the longitudinal and/or lateral direction, and may include portions positioned on or near the elastic members to regulate displacement, contraction, or separation of the elastic members.

By providing the stretchable regions near the side seals and fixing the sheet layers and elastic members through welded bonding sections, the diaper improves fit around the wearer’s waist and hips, suppresses wrinkling or twisting near the sealed sides, and enhances wearing comfort and appearance. The structure also improves manufacturing stability by reliably positioning the elastic members during production and by strengthening the regions adjacent to the side seal portions without substantially impairing elasticity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

The front outer member (12F) and the back outer member (12B) are joined to one another at laterally opposed side seal portions (12A) so as to define a waist opening and a pair of leg openings.

At least one of the front outer member (12F) and the back outer member (12B) includes a plurality of sheet layers, including a first sheet layer (12S) and a second sheet layer (12H), disposed in an overlapping relationship. One or more elastic members (19) are arranged between the first sheet layer (12S) and the second sheet layer (12H). The elastic members (19) extend in a lateral direction of the article and are configured to impart stretchability to stretchable regions (A2, A3) of the corresponding outer member.

Each elastic member (19) includes fixed ends (19f) secured to the sheet layers (12S, 12H). The fixed ends (19f) are attached by bonding sections (20) formed between the sheet layers. The bonding sections (20) may comprise adhesive-bonded portions, heat-sealed portions, ultrasonic-sealed portions, or combinations thereof. The bonding sections (20) are arranged to hold the elastic members (19) in a stretched or contractible state, thereby forming the stretchable regions (A2, A3) in the front outer member (12F) and/or the back outer member (12B).

In certain embodiments, the stretchable regions comprise a waist-side stretchable region (A2) and a lower stretchable region (A3), each including a plurality of the elastic members (19) extending between the side seal portions (12A). The elastic members (19) are intermittently or continuously fixed to at least one of the sheet layers (12S, 12H) at the bonding sections (20), and portions of the elastic members located between the fixed ends (19f) are capable of contraction to gather the sheet layers and provide an elastic fit around a wearer.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the invention disclosed by a patent for a pants-type disposable diaper, including the arrangement of stretchable regions adjacent side seals and the configuration of elastic stretchable members and sheet bonding sections.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent discloses a **pants-type disposable diaper** designed to improve fit and appearance around the wearer’s waist and hips, especially near the **side seal portions** where the front and rear waist regions are joined.

The diaper includes:

- a **front waist region** and a **rear waist region**;
- paired **side seal portions** joining the front and rear waist regions to form a pants shape;
- a **waist opening** and a pair of **leg openings**; and
- an absorbent body extending between the front and rear regions.

A key feature is the provision of **stretchable regions positioned adjacent to the side seal portions**. These stretchable regions are arranged in the waist-circumferential direction so that the diaper can expand and contract around the wearer’s body, helping the diaper fit snugly without excessive tightening or wrinkling near the side seams.

Within these stretchable regions, the diaper has a laminate structure including sheet materials, such as an inner sheet and an outer sheet, with a plurality of **elastic stretchable members** disposed between them. The elastic members extend generally in the **waist-surrounding direction**, parallel to one another, so that the waist region can stretch laterally.

The sheets are joined by multiple **sheet bonding sections**. These bonding sections are arranged at intervals rather than continuously, so the elastic members can contract and form gathers while the sheets remain connected in a controlled pattern. In particular:

- the elastic members are positioned between opposed sheet layers;
- the sheet bonding sections are distributed in the stretchable region at spaced locations;
- the bonding sections may be arranged in rows or patterns between or around the elastic members; and
- the bonding pattern helps regulate how the sheets gather when the elastics contract.

By arranging the stretchable regions adjacent the side seals and by coordinating the positions of the elastic members with the sheet bonding sections, the invention provides a diaper that has improved stretchability, better body conformity, reduced stiffness or bulk near the side seals, and a neater external appearance when worn.
